library_head.description:
This event is an in-person screening of the Grow-It-Together Garden Program.

This online garden club is for adults 50 years and older who are interested in hydroponic gardening. Join others to learn tips from a Mather coach who will discuss a variety of garden topics and answer any questions that come up during the growing process. Experience the simple joys of gardening with fresh herbs and vegetables in the comfort of your home with our Grow-It-Together (G.I.T.) Garden Kits. You can learn more about the program by visiting this link. Registration for kits is currently open. You can still attend these club meetings even if you do not have a kit. library_head.title: Adult Book Club: Orbital (2023)
library_head.description:
Join our book club for a discussion of a different book each month. This month's book is this year's One Book, One Chicago selection, Orbital.

A slender novel of epic power and the winner of the Booker Prize 2024, Orbital deftly snapshots one day in the lives of six women and men traveling through space. Selected for one of the last space station missions of its kind before the program is dismantled, these astronauts and cosmonauts—from America, Russia, Italy, Britain, and Japan—have left their lives behind to travel at a speed of over seventeen thousand miles an hour as the earth reels below. We glimpse moments of their earthly lives through brief communications with family, their photos and talismans; we watch them whip up dehydrated meals, float in gravity-free sleep, and exercise in regimented routines to prevent atrophying muscles; we witness them form bonds that will stand between them and utter solitude. Most of all, we are with them as they behold and record their silent blue planet. Their experiences of sixteen sunrises and sunsets and the bright, blinking constellations of the galaxy are at once breathtakingly awesome and surprisingly intimate.

Profound and contemplative, Orbital is a moving elegy to our environment and planet.

sample.title: Virtual Writing Club for Adults (Workshop Session)
sample.description:
Looking for writing inspiration? A chance to connect with others who write? A place to share your work and get feedback?

Join us on Zoom for a monthly writing circle! No experience is necessary. We believe that every person has stories to tell, and we would love to hear them.

Virtual Writing Circle will provide opportunities for both creative writing exercise and opportunities for deeper sharing and peer review.

  • Odd months will focus on writing prompts & inspiration: sessions typically include a brief writing warm-up with time to share, then a longer writing period based on a prompt or creative lesson with time to share
  • Even months will focus on peer review and feedback: register to receive instructions & brief homework from hosts ahead of the class!

Registration required to receive meeting link.

How To Attend
This event takes place through an online meeting platform. Please register by 10 a.m. the day before the event. You’ll receive an email with a link to the secure virtual meeting ~24 hours before the meeting. By registering for this event, you agree to abide by the Library Use Guidelines.

Chicago Public Library cannot collect personal information online from kids 0 to 13. A parent or guardian’s e-mail address must be used to register. 

This event uses a third-party website and may be hosted by an organization CPL has partnered with. We recommend you review the privacy policies of any third-party sites before providing them with any personal data. For more information, please see our Website Privacy Statement.

Questions about attending online events? Check out our Events FAQs.

Accessibility
Automatic transcription is included in all CPL events using Zoom. Need live captioning for this event? Please call (312) 747-4072 or email access@chipublib.org. Requests for live captioning must be made at least 14 business days before the event.

sample.title: Cozy or Cluttered?
sample.description:
‘Tis the season when our thoughts turn inward to home and comfort. The time is ripe for rest, peace and the pleasure of an absorbing book, a great movie, warm drinks and that special throw wrapped around your legs. Hygge, the Danish art of Living Cozy, has captured our hearts with visions of warmth, friendships, nourishing food, and candlelight.

But WAIT! As you settle in for a relaxing afternoon or evening, your eyes wander to a pile of papers that need attention, a shelf of knickknacks that haven’t been dusted since Spring Cleaning 2025, that box of stuff that belongs to one of your adult kids. Suddenly, the Hygge moment is gone. You try not to care and promise yourself that someday very soon, you’ll get to all of it. Clutter sabotages happiness by making your stuff more important than the self-care of living with ease.

Let’s have a cozy conversation about the “Stuff of our Lives.” We’ll share strategies for making the “Fourth Quarter” more Hygge and less cluttered.

Hosted by Feng Shui practitioner Lyn Nené. She has studied with Feng Shui Masters from The Wind and Water School of Feng Shui as well as The Feng Shui Institute of America.

Registration is recommended but not required. Please register online or at the Edgewater Branch reference desk.

Held in partnership with Edgewater Village Chicago.

sample.title: Jazz Institute of Chicago presents: Lost in Space with Kevin King
sample.description:
Lost In Space is a series inspired by astronomy and musicians who embody the idea of space. Chicago woodwindist and composer Kevin King presents a series of compositions that represent different aspects of space and how we as human beings are reflected in that. Alumnus of the Jazz Institute of Chicago (JIC) Jazz Links program, King will be performing this limited series of concerts across the city.

Kevin King honed his skills on the Chicago music scene under the tutelage of Chicago Legends Willie Pickens, Orbert Davis, and Diane Ellis. King has played all over the country with countless artists including Arturo Sandoval, Lauryn Hill, The Fugees, The Temptations, Marquis Hill, Art Ensemble of Chicago, Buddy Guy, etc. King is influenced by every sound known and unknown to man, which creates a sound unlike anything you have heard before. King has also written compositions inspired by some of the works of Wayne Shorter and John Coltrane. The original compositions King writes are in many ways a symbol of the values King lives by. An urgency to improve the world we live in with the art of sound creation, experimentation, and exploration. The music is a reflection of the world itself.
